subject.title: feat(queue): persist followup queues across gateway restarts

question: Should follow-up queues intentionally prefer at-least-once replay after a gateway crash, accepting a possible duplicate if the process dies after external delivery but before the SQLite acknowledgement write?
rationale: No local persistence protocol can generally prove exactly-once delivery across an external channel side effect without a channel-specific idempotency contract; the choice trades a possible duplicate against the prior silent loss of queued work.

options.title: Accept at-least-once recovery
options.body: Keep the SQLite acknowledgement ordering, state the duplicate-on-crash boundary plainly, and treat avoiding silent queue loss as the priority.

options.title: Require channel idempotency
options.body: Pause this PR until the delivery layer can persist and enforce a durable idempotency key across each supported channel.

options.title: Limit the feature scope
options.body: Persist queue state but defer automatic replay until a narrower delivery-semantics design is approved.

recommendation.title: Accept at-least-once recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the SQLite acknowledgement ordering, state the duplicate-on-crash boundary plainly, and treat avoiding silent queue loss as the priority.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline connects this person to adjacent gateway restart work and the design choice spans gateway lifecycle and message delivery semantics.
